Controls: a generator that emits `CK_{ACCT}_*` as a partial-token wildcard, or a `deny` entry carving out of a broader allow, fails this arm, which is the failure mode partial wildcards and deny-precedence produce on a real server; feeding the generator an out-of-lexicon host id such as `box_a-b` makes it refuse at derivation with the offending token named rather than emitting a golden-shaped file; and a client with a valid JWT connecting with the default inbox prefix connects and is then refused on its reply subscription, proving the grant is matched against the configured prefix and not against a library default.

Constants arms, each with its discriminating control. Account encoding: the naming crate refuses `box_a-b` at derivation with the offending token named and accepts `box_a_b`; control, two accepted account tokens produce two distinct sets of stream and bucket names, so the arm would fail under any mapping that collapsed the pair. Stream bindings: the limits crate accepts the five literal bindings in constraints and refuses a `CK_{ACCT}_EFFECT` configured with the wider `ck.{acct}.effect.>` filter, naming the overlap with `CK_{ACCT}_EFFECT_DEAD`; it also refuses a durable consumer configuration whose filter subject is not a subset of its stream's binding, naming the filter and the binding; controls, both refusals happen in the crate before the server is asked, and a rig run that lets each bad configuration through reproduces the server's own create-time refusal (overlapping filters at stream create, `JSConsumerFilterNotSubsetErr` at consumer create), so crate and server agree on which configurations are illegal. Backoff: a link held down past the ceiling emits `bus.link.backoff_ceiling` once per escalation; control, a link that reconnects before the ceiling emits none. Cold-start herd: 32 participants connect against the vault-side admission limiter (or its rig-local stand-in, recording `ckcred-admission-limit-unlanded` for the vault half) driven by an injected clock with all 32 requests queued, no 1 s sliding window at the limiter exceeds 16 admissions, `bus.connect.admission_delayed` fired at least once, and every participant reaches an authenticated publish with none reporting `Unavailable` from the connect-path sign deadline; controls, the same herd with the limiter removed exceeds the window bound, so the arm measures the limiter and not the jitter; a rate-16/s burst-16 token bucket substituted for the sliding window admits a seventeenth sign inside the first window and fails the arm, which is the discriminator that fixes the limiter's rule rather than its nominal rate; and a client that ignores the reported retry-after exhausts its connect retries, which is the failure mode a per-process bucket would have hidden. Sign deadline: a connect whose `credential.sign` exceeds 2 s after 3 retries reports `Unavailable` and enters backoff rather than hanging; control, a sign returning inside the deadline neither reports `Unavailable` nor enters backoff, and a sign delayed by a reported `Clamped` admission consumes no retry. Body resolution: a replayed delivery whose body is gone from the owning store is reported `Absent`, naked, and terminally disposed with reason `body_absent` — never acked as delivered; a digest mismatch is quarantined and reported; control, a present body whose digest matches is delivered and acked, so neither path is reachable by a consumer that quarantines everything. Terminal disposition: cap exhaustion publishes the dead-letter record to `ck.{acct}.effect.dead` before `term()`, the record is consumed on `CK_{ACCT}_EFFECT_DEAD` by the `c_ckbus_dead` consumer F-PROV created, the record appears exactly once there and raises the delivery count of no `CK_{ACCT}_EFFECT` item — the observable that the dead-letter subject is outside the work queue's binding — and a crash injected between the two leaves the item redeliverable with the record present and deduplicated on message id; control, an item under the cap is redelivered and never appears on the dead-letter stream. Retention ordering: a stream configuration whose max-age exceeds the declared store retention is refused by the limits crate; control, the shipped 24 h PEER max-age against the 48 h peer store retention is accepted.


## non_goals

- The bus module is not built here. Operator ruling on ask_0379ad21, 2026-09-18: SUBC owns it; it is a standalone repository and Cargo workspace with its own store, sibling to the other CortexKit repositories as entorhinal is, and it is supervised under the module id `ckbus` (working repository name `ckbus`; both names await owner confirmation and no build, test or config step may reference an operator-machine absolute path such as `~/Work/Projects/CortexKit/`). It mints per-process credentials in Claustrum, writes and deletes the census keys, executes the three-step revocation, subscribes to the supervisor's spawn event stream, runs the reconciliation sweep, hosts the sentinel probe, and holds both the plane's NATS credential and the system-account user. The spawn event shape is SUBC's to define with the stream. This repository consumes it as an external dependency and never creates a crate for it; the acceptance arms that exercise it (A2 child observation, A3 in full, A5 leaf credential) carry the recorded-skip reason `bus-module-unlanded` until it lands. A2's gating half does not wait on it: it runs against the rig-local signing-record fixture named in acceptance_sketch.
- Building on other seats' planes from this repository: SUBC's `protocol: "none"` mode, spawn event stream and per-process principal; CALLO's roster column, fed-wire hello field, `callosum.hub_read` and device re-key path; CKCRED's signing-record kinds, JWT issuer shape and the install bootstrap that mints the box and system account keys. These are their build items, dispatched to their seats with this spec's acceptance as the contract. Slices minted here fence prefrontal only: the trait crate and in-memory backend, the NATS backend, the naming-and-grant crate (including the limits check and the generated permission files), and the acceptance rig including the grant-conformance arm. The sentinel probe's behaviour is specified here and implemented in the bus module's repository; this repository owns only its acceptance arm.
- Porting any workload. Rooms, wakes, peer deliveries and effect intents each move in their own later slice, in that order, with effect intents last or never. Each port slice declares its owning store's retention against its stream's max-age and proves its ids are inside the token lexicon or maps them.
- Replacing the tool wire or Callosum's fed-wire. Module calls and fed re-export stay where they are.
- Hosted service build-out (accounts hosting, billing, leaf enrollment UI). This cut makes the local shape hosted-compatible and enforces the account-token, account-field and one-hub obligations in constraints; it does not stand the hosted hub up.
- A multi-backend queue abstraction over NATS, Cloudflare Queues, SQS or similar (operator ruling, room #10).
- Push to a sleeping phone; APNs with the sealed payload stays the notification plane.
- Bus health inside the subc supervisor; the sentinel probe owns it, and nothing it reports gates spawning.
- Renaming `{acct}` at pairing, or any migration of streams, buckets and durable cursors that a rename would require. `{acct}` is fixed for the life of the box (constraints, Names and grants); if CALLO's ceremony cannot hold that, it reopens this spec rather than being absorbed by a port slice.
- Claiming that a child process cannot authenticate to the local bus. This cut claims seed absence on enumerated surfaces only; the child-denial mechanism is owed by SUBC and CKCRED (constraints, Credentials).
